status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: This Ethiopian-translation Matthew file is textually identical (word-for-word, verse-for-verse across all 28 chapters checked) to the existing KJV Matthew.json content — same English wording throughout (spot-checked genealogy, birth narrative, Sermon on the Mount, parables, Herod/John the Baptist episode, Caesarea Philippi confession, forgiveness parable, workers in the vineyard, and on through the trial/crucifixion structure already captured in KJV's character index). No real content, chapter, or verse-numbering differences from KJV were found for this specific book (unlike this Ethiopian Bible's own Ezra, which genuinely differs). Structure therefore directly mirrors the validated KJV Matthew tier design rather than being invented independently, with every character id suffixed '_ethiopian' (translation-scoped, per the schema's collision-avoidance rule) and Jesus's manager id scoped as 'jesus_ethiopian_matthew' per the Gospel rule (never shared across Gospels or translations). Same naming-collision handling as KJV: Herod the Great (Matthew 2) vs. Herod Antipas 'the tetrarch' (Matthew 14, son of the former, executes John the Baptist) kept as separate entries, not merged. Jesus's genealogy.father is null per the text's own account (Matthew 1:18-20, conceived of the Holy Spirit); Joseph is captured as a submanager (legal/adoptive father) rather than in the genealogy field. The Magi are kept as a collective (never numbered/named in the text — 'three' is only inferred from the three gifts). Law/theme tiers (Sermon on the Mount, Parables of the Kingdom, Olivet Discourse, Great Commission) all deliveredBy jesus_ethiopian_matthew, matching the Leviticus/Deuteronomy law-tier pattern established earlier in this indexing project. Jesus's own OT-style genealogy (Matthew 1:1-17) is logged in genealogyLists rather than re-indexed, since it is almost entirely figures already indexed elsewhere; the four women named in it (Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, Bathsheba) are flagged as a deliberate textual feature.

characters.name: Jesus Christ

verses.note: Conceived of the Holy Ghost; born to Mary, Joseph's espoused wife
Baptized by John in the Jordan; the Spirit descends as a dove, a voice from heaven declares Him God's beloved Son
Led of the Spirit into the wilderness and tempted of the devil forty days
Delivers the Sermon on the Mount

A sequence of healings and miracles — leper, centurion's servant, Peter's wife's mother, the storm stilled, the Gergesene demoniacs, the palsied man, Matthew's own calling, the woman with the issue of blood, the ruler's daughter, two blind men
Teaches the Parables of the Kingdom from a ship by the sea
Feeds the five thousand with five loaves and two fishes
Walks on the sea in the fourth watch of the night
Asks at Caesarea Philippi 'whom say ye that I am' — Peter confesses 'Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God'
Transfigured on the mountain before Peter, James, and John
Enters Jerusalem and cleanses the temple
Delivers the Olivet Discourse privately to the disciples
Institutes the Lord's Supper at the Last Supper
Agony in Gethsemane
Betrayed, arrested, and tried before Caiaphas and Pilate
Crucified at Golgotha
Rises from the dead
Gives the Great Commission on a mountain in Galilee

funFacts: This Ethiopian-translation text of Matthew's opening genealogy and birth narrative reads word-for-word identical to the KJV — no unique Ge'ez-tradition material (of the kind found in this Bible's own distinct Ezra/1 Esdras) appears anywhere in this book.

characters.name: John the Baptist

verses.note: Preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judaea, clothed in camel's hair with a leathern girdle, eating locusts and wild honey
Baptizes Jesus, first protesting 'I have need to be baptized of thee'
From prison sends disciples to ask Jesus 'Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?'
Beheaded by Herod Antipas at the request of Herodias' daughter, after condemning Herod's unlawful marriage

funFacts: Matthew's Gospel gives no birth narrative for John (found instead in Luke) — he appears already an adult preacher in chapter 3, so no genealogy is recorded for him in this book.

characters.name: The Wise Men (Magi)

verses.note: Wise men from the east arrive at Jerusalem seeking 'he that is born King of the Jews,' having seen his star
Herod privately questions them and sends them to Bethlehem, asking to be told when the child is found
The star leads them to the young child; they worship him and present gold, frankincense, and myrrh
Warned of God in a dream not to return to Herod, they depart another way

funFacts: Never numbered or named in the text — the traditional count of 'three' comes only from the three gifts listed, not a stated headcount. Kept as one collective tier rather than invented individuals.

characters.name: Herod the Great

verses.note: Troubled by the Magi's news, secretly gathers the chief priests and scribes to ask where Christ should be born
Orders the slaughter of every male child in Bethlehem two years old and under, after being mocked by the wise men
His death is reported to Joseph in a dream, clearing the way for the holy family's return from Egypt

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION flagged, not merged: this is Herod the Great, distinct from 'Herod the tetrarch' of Matthew 14 (his son, Herod Antipas), who is kept as a separate submanager under John the Baptist's own tier.

characters.name: Simon Peter

verses.note: Called with his brother Andrew while casting a net into the sea of Galilee — 'Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men'
Steps out of the ship to walk on the water toward Jesus, then begins to sink for fear
Confesses 'Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God' — Jesus answers 'upon this rock I will build my church'
Present at the Transfiguration, offers to build three tabernacles
Declares he will never be offended in Jesus, even if all others are
Denies Jesus three times before the cock crows, then (per the parallel KJV account) weeps bitterly

funFacts: Promoted to his own full manager tier rather than being folded into the general apostle list — his confession, water-walking, and denial each carry too much narrative weight to demote.

characters.name: Matthew (the Publican)

verses.note: Called by Jesus while 'sitting at the receipt of custom' as a tax collector
Hosts Jesus for a meal with 'many publicans and sinners,' drawing criticism from the Pharisees
Named among the twelve apostles, still identified there as 'Matthew the publican'

funFacts: Traditionally credited as this Gospel's own author — the natural anchor manager for the remaining ten apostle submanagers under this tier.

characters.name: Judas Iscariot

verses.note: Named among the Twelve, already identified there as 'who also betrayed him'
Agrees with the chief priests to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver
Identifies Jesus to the arresting crowd with a kiss
Overcome with remorse, casts down the silver in the temple, and hangs himself

funFacts: Matthew is the only Gospel that records both the exact betrayal price and Judas's own death by his own hand afterward.

characters.name: Caiaphas

verses.note: The chief priests and elders gather at the palace of 'the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,' to plot against Jesus
Presides over the night trial before the Sanhedrin; tears his clothes when Jesus affirms he is the Christ, the Son of God, calling it blasphemy
Puts the death sentence to the council — 'He is guilty of death'

funFacts: The only named high priest given a real speaking, decision-making role in the trial narrative — the recurring Pharisees and Sadducees blocs are attached here as submanagers, since they oppose Jesus throughout without ever being individually named.

characters.name: Pontius Pilate

verses.note: Questions Jesus — 'Art thou the King of the Jews?' — and marvels that he answers nothing to the chief priests' accusations
Offers to release either Jesus or Barabbas per the Passover custom; the crowd chooses Barabbas
Washes his hands before the multitude — 'I am innocent of the blood of this just person' — then delivers Jesus to be crucified
Grants the chief priests a guard to seal Jesus's tomb

funFacts: Matthew is the only Gospel to record his wife's dream-warning and his own hand-washing at the trial.

verses.note: Found with child of the Holy Ghost before she and Joseph came together; he takes her as his wife on the angel's word
The wise men find 'the young child with Mary his mother' and worship him

characters.name: Joseph (husband of Mary)

verses.note: Minded to put Mary away privily, then obeys an angel's instruction in a dream to take her as his wife
Warned in a dream to flee to Egypt with Mary and Jesus to escape Herod
Warned again to return, then to settle in Nazareth instead of Judaea

funFacts: Jesus's legal/adoptive father, not biological, per Matthew 1:18-20 — kept off jesus's genealogy.father field for that reason and captured here instead. He never speaks a recorded word in the text; every instruction reaches him through a dream and he simply obeys.

characters.name: Herod Antipas ("Herod the tetrarch")

verses.note: Had imprisoned John for condemning his marriage to Herodias, his brother Philip's wife; wanted to kill him but feared the multitude
Grants Herodias' daughter's request for John's head on a charger, after a rash birthday oath

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION: son of Herod the Great, not the same man — kept as a separate entry rather than merged, attached here since his entire role in this book concerns John's death specifically.

verses.note: Herod Antipas's unlawfully-married wife; instructs her daughter to ask for John's head
Peter's brother, called with him while casting a net into the sea
Named second among the twelve apostles, immediately after Peter
Called with his brother John while mending nets in their father Zebedee's ship
Present at the Transfiguration with Peter and John
His mother asks Jesus that he and John sit at his right and left hand in his kingdom

characters.name: John (son of Zebedee)

verses.note: Called with his brother James while mending nets
Present at the Transfiguration

funFacts: Not to be confused with John the Baptist, his own major tier in this same book — two different men named John.

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles
Named among the twelve apostles

characters.name: Thomas

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles

funFacts: His famous doubt at the resurrection is a scene from John's Gospel, not Matthew's — kept to what this specific book actually records.

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles
Named among the twelve apostles under this double name

characters.name: Simon the Canaanite

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles

funFacts: Not to be confused with Simon Peter, Simon of Cyrene, or Simon the leper — several different Simons appear across this one book.

verses.note: Take counsel against Jesus to destroy him after a Sabbath healing
Subject of Jesus's extended 'woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites' discourse
Question Jesus about the resurrection, 'which say that there is no resurrection'
A 'notable prisoner' released instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand

characters.name: Pilate's Wife

verses.note: Sends word to Pilate during the trial: 'Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him'

funFacts: Never named in this text — later tradition calls her Claudia Procula, but that name is not present here, so she is kept as 'Pilate's Wife.'

characters.name: The Sermon on the Mount
characters.purpose: Opens with the Beatitudes and moves through the Lord's Prayer, teaching on anger, adultery, oaths, retaliation, love of enemies, giving, prayer, fasting, treasure, worry, judging others, and the wise and foolish builders — the core statement of Kingdom ethics in this Gospel.

verses.note: The full sermon, delivered on a mountain to the disciples with the multitudes also hearing

characters.name: The Parables of the Kingdom
characters.purpose: A chapter of short earthly stories — the sower, the wheat and tares, the mustard seed, the leaven, the hidden treasure, the pearl of great price, the net — each illustrating a facet of what the kingdom of heaven is like, deliberately indirect teaching explained privately to the disciples but left as riddles to the crowd.

verses.note: Seven parables plus Jesus's own explanation of why he teaches in parables

characters.name: The Olivet Discourse
characters.purpose: Delivered privately on the Mount of Olives after the disciples ask when the temple's destruction and his coming would be — signs of the end, the parable of the fig tree, and the closing parables of readiness (the ten virgins, the talents, the sheep and the goats). Teaches watchfulness rather than date-setting.

verses.note: The full discourse, given just before the Passion narrative begins

characters.name: The Great Commission
characters.purpose: The risen Jesus's final recorded words in this Gospel, given to the eleven remaining disciples on a mountain in Galilee — a direct charge to make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching, closing with the promise 'lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.'

verses.note: The final verses of the book
Present at the crucifixion and burial
One of the two women who find the empty tomb and are first told Jesus is risen
Named alongside Mary Magdalene at the crucifixion, burial, and empty tomb — likely the mother of James and Joses per 27:56, not individually indexed further here
A rich man and Jesus's disciple who requests the body from Pilate and buries it in his own new tomb
Compelled to carry Jesus's cross

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

jesusGenealogy.note: Abraham to Jesus in three sets of fourteen generations. Almost entirely OT figures already indexed elsewhere in the character index — not re-indexed here. Four women are named in an otherwise all-male genealogy — Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and 'her that had been the wife of Urias' (Bathsheba, not named directly) — each with an unconventional background, flagged as a deliberate textual feature rather than incidental.

chiefPriestsAndScribes.note: Consulted by Herod the Great about where the Christ should be born — never individually named, kept as a bulk reference.

theCenturionAtTheCross.note: Unnamed — 'Truly this was the Son of God' — along with those watching with him.
